question: Protecting citizens’ health is a top priority. Recently the 60th session of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC-60) approved the drafting of a Special Report on Climate Change and Cities. On 18 January 2024, the European Scientific Advisory Board on Climate Change (EUSABCC) published a report entitled ‘Towards EU climate neutrality: progress, policy gaps and opportunities’1.

In this report, the EUSABCC recommends a series of actions to put the EU on track towards climate neutrality. Does the Commission envisage contributing to the IPCC special report or updating/aligning the EUSABCC recommendations in order to protect citizens’ lives?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.4.2024) EU climate policy is science-based and informed predominantly by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) reports, which constitute the most authoritative assessments of climate science. They are written by leading experts in the field.

The IPCC called for member governments and observer organisations to nominate experts who will draft the outline of the Special Report on Climate Change and Cities, and the expert meeting will be held in 2024. Authors are selected based on their expertise and considering the representation of different regions and genders. The report is expected to be delivered in early 2027.

The EU, represented by the Commission, is an observer organisation to the IPCC, and is included in the review process of the reports and attends IPCC sessions. The EU contributes to the IPCC by both financial support to the organisation and by funding research that is assessed by the IPCC. In the sixth Assessment Report1, EU-funded research was a key contributor to IPCC assessments.

The Commission welcomes the report of the European Scientific Advisory Board on Climate Change on progress and policy consistency towards EU climate neutrality that it published the 18 January 2024. It is a timely and comprehensive report that provides solid input for the climate programme of the next Commission.

The findings and recommendations of the report are generally in line with the Commission’s own analysis as contained in the Climate Action Progress Report2 and the assessment of Member States’ National Energy and Climate Plans3.. The Commission will reflect on the report and consider its advice, including with a view to protect citizens’ lives.
